What services does IBM Cloud® Internet Services (CIS) offer?

IBM Cloud® Internet Services (CIS), powered by Cloudflare, offers three key capabilities to enhance your workflow: security, reliability, and performance. After accessing the CIS user interface, you can explore the features associated with each of these capabilities. CIS provides a fast, reliable, and secure internet service for customers running their businesses on IBM Cloud.

DNS servers translate domain names, like ibm.com, into their corresponding IP addresses, which users typically don't need to know. The DNS system retrieves this IP address and hostname information from a network of interconnected DNS servers across the internet, much like how someone would search for a location using a phone book or map. Computers on a network identify each other using IP addresses. To simplify interactions within a computer network, people can utilize the Domain Name System (DNS) to link user-friendly domain names to IP addresses, resembling a phonebook. Additionally, a DNS can associate various types of information, not just computer network addresses, with domain names.

DNSSEC is a technology that digitally signs DNS data to ensure its validity. To eliminate vulnerabilities on the internet, DNSSEC must be implemented at every stage of the lookup process, from the root zone to the final domain name (for example, www.icann.org).
DNSSEC adds a layer of authentication to the internet's DNS infrastructure, which is otherwise insecure. Secure DNS ensures that users are directed to your web server when they enter your domain name in a web browser. DNSSEC enables resolvers to cryptographically verify the data received from authoritative servers. DNS service resolvers support DNSSEC for public domains, forwarding requests to public resolvers that also support DNSSEC. For private zones, since the authority lies within IBM Cloud, records are retrieved using secure protocols, ensuring the same level of privacy and security that DNSSEC provides for public zones.
